registry_info.name: datastructures
registry_info.description: 3D visualizations of fundamental and advanced data structures — from linked lists and binary trees through B-trees, tries, and spatial partitioning. Each artifact makes abstract memory layouts tangible and traversal algorithms visible.
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Abstract data types, algorithmic complexity (Big-O), tree balancing invariants, hashing theory, spatial indexing, graph representations

binary_trees.name: Binary Trees
binary_trees.description: Interactive binary tree visualization showing insertion, deletion, and traversal orders (in-order, pre-order, post-order). Nodes light up as each traversal algorithm visits them, making the recursive structure visible.
binary_trees.qfep_connection: Trees as hierarchical F-structures — each node's position encodes a decision, each traversal order reveals different information. The tree IS a compressed representation of sorted data: O(log n) access through recursive bisection.

bst_visualization.name: Binary Search Tree
bst_visualization.description: Binary search tree with dynamic insertion maintaining the BST invariant: left child < parent < right child. Watch how ordered insertion creates degenerate trees while balanced insertion creates efficient ones.

bsp_trees.name: BSP Trees
bsp_trees.description: Binary Space Partitioning tree visualization — recursive halfplane splits dividing space into convex regions. The algorithm behind Doom's rendering and modern collision detection.

btree_visualization.name: B-Tree
btree_visualization.description: B-tree visualization showing multi-key nodes that split and merge to maintain balance. The data structure behind databases and filesystems — every query you've ever run touched one.

fenwick_tree.name: Fenwick Tree
fenwick_tree.description: Binary Indexed Tree for efficient prefix sum queries. Shows how clever bit manipulation enables O(log n) range queries and updates — compact elegance in a tree that isn't really a tree.

graph_structures.name: Graph Structures
graph_structures.description: Side-by-side comparison of directed and undirected graphs with adjacency visualization. Nodes and edges as the universal language for relationships — from social networks to circuit diagrams.
graph_structures.qfep_connection: Graphs are the most general F-structure — any relationship between any entities. Directed edges encode asymmetric information flow; undirected edges encode mutual coupling. The graph IS the topology of E(S) propagation.

hash_maps.name: Hash Maps
hash_maps.description: Hash table visualization with buckets, collision chains, and hash function mapping. Watch keys distribute across buckets and see why a good hash function means O(1) lookup while a bad one degrades to O(n).
hash_maps.qfep_connection: Hash maps trade space-entropy for time-order — using a hash function to scatter keys uniformly across buckets achieves O(1) access at the cost of memory overhead. A good hash maximizes E(S) in the bucket distribution to minimize F in the lookup.

heap_operations.name: Heap Operations
heap_operations.description: Min-heap and max-heap with sift-up and sift-down operations animated. The structure behind priority queues — always know your most important element in O(1), insert and extract in O(log n).
heap_operations.qfep_connection: Heaps maintain partial order at the edge of chaos — not fully sorted (low λ), not random (high λ), but just ordered enough to know the extremum in O(1). The minimum viable F-structure for priority access.

linked_lists.name: Linked Lists
linked_lists.description: Singly and doubly linked list visualization with node insertion, deletion, and pointer traversal. The simplest dynamic data structure — nodes connected by references, not memory layout.

quadtrees_octrees.name: Quadtrees & Octrees
quadtrees_octrees.description: Side-by-side spatial partitioning: quadtree subdivides 2D space, octree subdivides 3D. Watch regions split as points accumulate — the backbone of collision detection, LOD systems, and spatial databases.
quadtrees_octrees.qfep_connection: Adaptive spatial partitioning — subdivide only where complexity accumulates. Dense regions get finer cells (higher F resolution), sparse regions stay coarse (lower F cost). The structure adapts its own resolution to match local E(S) density.

redblack_visualization.name: Red-Black Tree
redblack_visualization.description: Self-balancing BST with red-black coloring invariants. Rotations and recolorings maintain O(log n) height — the tree behind Java's TreeMap and Linux's scheduler.
redblack_visualization.qfep_connection: Self-balancing as continuous F-minimization — rotations and recolorings restore balance after every insertion, keeping the tree at its F-optimal O(log n) height. The invariants ARE the F-model: constraints that prevent entropy accumulation.

segment_tree.name: Segment Tree
segment_tree.description: Segment tree for range queries (min, max, sum) with lazy propagation. Each node stores an aggregate of its interval — answer any range query in O(log n) after O(n) construction.

suffix_array_tree.name: Suffix Array & Tree
suffix_array_tree.description: Side-by-side suffix array and suffix tree for string indexing. The structures that make text search instantaneous — every substring query answered in O(m) regardless of text length.

trie_operations.name: Trie Operations
trie_operations.description: Prefix tree (trie) with insertion and search animated character-by-character. The structure behind autocomplete and spell checkers — shared prefixes become shared paths.
trie_operations.qfep_connection: Tries achieve F-minimization through prefix sharing — common beginnings are stored once, branching only where strings diverge. The trie IS a compression of the string set: minimum redundancy, maximum structural reuse.

union_find.name: Union-Find
union_find.description: Disjoint set union with path compression and union by rank. Watch components merge in near-constant time — the algorithm that makes Kruskal's MST efficient and connected component detection trivial.
union_find.qfep_connection: Path compression as F-minimization in real-time — every find operation flattens the tree, making future operations faster. The structure optimizes itself through use, reducing its own entropy cost with each query.
